plugin.name: Hanshuang Pojia
plugin.description: Statically triage APK, AAB, IPA, DEX, ELF, PE, Mach-O and archive samples: format, manifest facts, permissions, exported components, native hardening, embedded secrets and a scored report — no execution, no external toolchain.
skill.name: Hanshuang Pojia — engagement executor
skill.description: Red-team and blue-team engagement executor: CTF challenges, ranges, AWD rounds, license and activation reversing, malware triage and incident response. Carries the workbench kit 2.0 protocol: lab mode, deployment verification, and the seep / IDA MCP toolchain. Execution-first — every reply opens with the artifact.

panel.handoff.prompt: Triage {{path}} statically. It is {{reason}}, so the plugin's own reader cannot open it — use your shell tools instead: hash it, identify the container and its entries, pull the notable strings (URLs, hosts, script names, embedded executables) and report each conclusion with evidence plus what you could not see. Never execute the sample.

risk.advice.A: Nothing beyond informational rules matched. Keep the routine checks — signature, permissions, embedded endpoints — before shipping.
risk.advice.B: A few low-impact issues. Fix them in the next build; none of them changes what the app can reach on the device.
risk.advice.C: Review before trusting this build. At least one medium rule touches data access or exported surface.
risk.advice.D: Treat as untrusted until reviewed. Dangerous permissions or exported components combine into real device-level exposure.
risk.advice.E: Treat as hostile. Multiple critical rules matched; do not install or run it on a device you care about.
risk.note: Score is a weighted rule sum, not a probability.
findings.empty.title: No rule matched
findings.empty.body: Nothing here crossed an informational threshold. Digging further in chat can still turn up endpoints or library versions the rules cannot judge.

manifest.noPermissions: No permission entries in this manifest.
manifest.noComponents: No component entries in this manifest.
manifest.note.axml: Binary AXML is read, never rewritten. The panel will not produce an edited manifest.
entropy.null.title: No bytes in memory
entropy.null.body: Entropy comes from the sample the panel read. Open a report from the library and re-run the analysis to get the profile.
entropy.note: 0 = flat/repetitive, 8 = indistinguishable from random. Compression or encryption shows up as a long high run; it is not proof of malware by itself.
entropy.bucketCount.hint: More buckets localise hot spots; fewer smooth the curve.
signature.none.title: No signature block
signature.none.body: This format has no APK signing block, or the archive has no manifest pointing at one.
signature.v1.detail: JAR signing over META-INF. Compatible with every Android version, weakest against tampering.
signature.v2.detail: Whole-file digest in the APK signing block. Required by Android 7 and later.
signature.v3.detail: Key rotation support, Android 9 and later.
signature.noScheme: The manifest does not name a scheme digest.
signature.limit.title: What the panel does not do
signature.limit.body: The panel reports structure only: it does not parse the certificate, resolve the signer identity or verify the digests. A present scheme means the block exists, not that the signer is trustworthy.
signature.limit.how: Ask the conversation to run apksigner verify (or codesign -dv for an IPA) and explain the signer it reports.

compare.needTwo.body: Analyse two samples in this panel first. Only reports from this session carry full details; the library keeps summaries.
compare.sameFindings: Same rule set; {{count}} finding(s) still match.
compare.pickTwo.title: Pick both sides
compare.pickTwo.body: Choose a base and a comparison report above.

selfcheck.tools.body: jadx, apktool and radare2 do not run inside the plugin process, so the panel cannot see their versions or call them. That is deliberate: the market package has no shell and has to stay small.

guide.step.read.body: Score, grade and each matched rule with its evidence, plus the limits of what was read.
guide.step.ask.title: Ask in chat

guide.step.export.title: Hand it on
guide.step.export.body: Save the report as Markdown or JSON, or let the agent write it up in the conversation.
guide.can.title: Two lanes
guide.can.panel.engine: Run the bundled engine on project files up to 32 MiB.
guide.can.panel.report: Score, findings, manifest, entropy, signature and a byte-level diff.
guide.can.panel.strings: Extract and classify strings without leaving the renderer.
guide.can.panel.compare: Diff two reports analysed in this session.
guide.can.chat.toolchain: Check jadx / apktool / radare2, and route deeper work through the kit's seep / IDA MCP servers when they answer.
guide.can.chat.explain: Explain a rule, a library version or an endpoint in context.
guide.can.chat.split: Work on samples outside the project or above the read cap.
guide.can.chat.disasm: Disassemble a byte range or list symbols for deeper work.
guide.limit.title: Limits
guide.limit.execute: The sample is never executed, unpacked to disk or uploaded.
guide.limit.network: No network access at all — the panel works offline.
guide.limit.size: One file per analysis, up to 32 MiB (the host's cap).
guide.limit.scope: Files must live inside the open project folder.
guide.limit.tools: No bundled jadx / apktool / radare2, and no shell inside the panel.
strings.null.title: Strings need a live analysis
strings.null.body: The panel keeps sample bytes only for reports it analysed itself. Re-open this sample from the workbench to extract strings.
strings.minLength.hint: Shorter strings are dropped before classification.
strings.limit.hint: Caps how many strings are extracted per sample.
disasm.unsupported.no-sample.title: No sample loaded
disasm.unsupported.no-sample.body: Deep disassembly works on the bytes the panel already holds, so open a native sample from the workbench first.
disasm.unsupported.no-facts.title: Not a native image
disasm.unsupported.no-facts.body: The address map needs a parsed ELF, PE or Mach-O header. Archives and mobile packages are unpacked by the tools in the chat instead.
disasm.unsupported.arch.title: No decoder for this architecture
disasm.unsupported.arch.body: The built-in decoder covers AArch64, x86 and x86-64. Other machines still get a full triage report, and the Agent can route the sample to radare2.
